elements.html:
Protocol: FB102-701

Phase: 1b

elements.name: question8
elements.html:
Opening

This study is testing a new treatment for Alopecia areata. Alopecia areata is an autoimmune condition that affects millions of people worldwide. Currently, there are limited treatment options available.

Alopecia areata is characterised by patchy hair loss on the scalp and happens when the immune system mistakenly attacks the hair follicles leading to hair loss. This usually happens when the hair follicles lose their natural immune protection, often triggered by stress, infection, or other factors.

elements.name: question9
elements.html:
Study Drug

This clinical trial is testing a new medicine, which is a type of antibody therapy. Normally, antibodies are made by the immune system to fight infections, but the study medication is made in a laboratory to target a specific part of the immune system response involved in alopecia areata. 

The aim of the study medication is to block these proteins from activating the immune cells that attack hair, while still allowing the rest of your immune system to function normally.

The study drug will be given through an Intravenous infusion — similar to how fluids or medications are administered via a drip in a hospital setting.

 

All participants in this study will receive either the study medication or placebo (a medication with no active ingredients). You will be assigned randomly (by chance) to receive either study medication or placebo. You will have a 3 in 4 chance of receiving the study medication and a 1 in 4 chance of receiving placebo. You cannot choose which study treatment you receive.

elements.name: question11
elements.html:
Study Design and Schedule 

The study will last for approximately 8 months and involves 13 clinic visits in total.

  • Your first visit will be a screening appointment, where the study team will assess your condition, review your medical history, and carry out safety tests (like bloodwork) to confirm your eligibility. You should allow up to around 2-3 hours of time for this visit. You can also expect your subsequent follow-up visits to take around 2 hours.
  • If eligible, you will return on Day 1 for your first dose of the study medication.
  • During the first 4 weeks, you will attend the clinic once a week for treatment ( Week 0, Week 1, Week 2, Week 3)
  • After that, you will attend the clinic once, every 2 weeks (Week 5, Week 7, Week 9, Week 11, Week 13).
  • A final treatment visit will take place around week 13.
  • After treatment ends, you will return for three follow-up visits to monitor your safety and progress (Week 16, Week 24 and Week 36) bringing you to the end of the study.
  • In total, you’ll receive 9 doses of the study medication, administered during visits 2 through to 10.  

 

Clinic Parking

There is very limited parking around the area so the clinic recommends taking an uber or using public transport.

elements.name: question64
elements.html:
Reimbursement

 

You will be reimbursed $400 for any reasonable travel, parking, meals and other expenses associated with each visit. 

 

This means if you attend all scheduled visits, you can receive up to $5200.

 

You may also receive up to $400 for any unscheduled visits the study team may deem necessary. These are not included in the total I just mentioned.

 

The study team will let you know if you're eligible for extra reimbursement related to rural travel.

elements.name: question65
elements.html:
Disclosure

 

Before we go any further, I want to explain exactly how the reimbursement works, so there are no surprises for you later. The reimbursement I just went through is what you'd receive if everything goes ahead as planned. That can look a bit different depending on what happens on the day. For example, if the doctor looks over your information early on and finds you're not eligible before you even get to the consent form, if you decide not to sign the consent form yourself, or if something doesn't line up with what you've told me today, you'd likely only get a partial amount, or in some cases nothing, instead of the full reimbursement.

 

That's actually a big part of why it matters that you're as accurate as possible with me right now. The doctor's early review is based on exactly what you tell me today, so the more accurate you are, the better your chances of making it all the way through screening and getting the full reimbursement.

elements.html:
For recruiters only- do not read to participants

The SALT score is used to estimate the severity of hair loss in people who have alopecia areata. For this study participants need a SALT score of 50% or greater which is defined as severe Alopecia areata.

The scalp is divided into four regions:

  • Left side: 18% of total scalp area
  • Right side: 18%
  • Top (vertex): 40%

  • Back (Occipital): 24%

     

Please click here for a guide on the visual representation of SALT scores and their corresponding hair loss percentages

 

To calculate the SALT score:

 

  1. Estimate the percentage of hair loss in each region using the questions below
  2. Put the SALT score calculator to determine their score

 

We will work through calculating the SALT score in the next few questions with the participant.

elements.name: question15
elements.html:
Please exclude the following medications

 

Within the past 6 months

  • Anti-cancer & autoimmune medications such as Rituximab (MabThera, Truxima, Rixathon)

     

Within the past 8 weeks

  • JAK inhibitors used for AA, rheumatoid arthritis and other autoimmune conditions (Tofacitinib (Xeljanz), Baricitinib (Olumiant), Ruxolitinib (Jakavi)

 

  • Biologics for autoimmune conditions  (Adalimumab (Humira), Etanercept (Enbrel), Infliximab (Remicade)

     

Within the past 8 weeks

  • Corticosteroids (oral or injectable) Prednisone (Deltasone), Prednisolone (Orapred, Predsol), Triamcinolone (Kenalog), Methylprednisolone (Depo-Medrol), azathioprine( Imuran)

 

  • Treatment for male or female pattern baldness/ thinning or enlarged prostrate (Finasteride (Propecia, Proscar), Dutasteride (Avodart)

 

  • Statins as a treatment for AA (Simvastatin (Zocor), Simvastatin + Ezetimibe (Inegy)

     

  • Oral minoxidil (Regaine (oral formulation)

     

  • Spironolactone if used specifically for AA (Aldactone)

     

  • Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injections (administered by a GP, nurse or dermatologist)

     

Within the past 4 weeks

  • Narrowband or broadband UVB therapy or tanning beds

     

  • Other laser or light based therapies 

     

  • Prescription chemical solutions or creams for treatment of AA (Diphenylcyclopropenone (DPCP),Squaric Acid Dibutylester (SADBE) or 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (DNCB)

     

  • Topical creams to stimulate hair growth such as Anthralin (Dritho-Scalp)

     

  • Liquid nitrogen cryotherapy (applied by dermatologist)

     

  • Topical treatments on affaected areas (Ruxolitinib, Tofacitinib), steroid creams (Betnovate, Dermovate), medicated shampoos, topical minoxidil (Regaine)

elements.name: question43
elements.html:
Please exclude the following:

 

  • Immunosuppressive conditions (e.g. HIV infection, Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C)
     

  • Severe infection within the 3 months prior to randomisation

     

  • Thyroid disease ( Hyperthyroidism, Hypothyroidism, Graves's disease

     

  • History of active tuberculosis (TB) or untreated or inadequately treated latent TB

     

  • Known or suspected acute systemic bacterial, viral, parasitic, or fungal infection; is currently, or has received systemic treatment for such within 30 days of Screening

     

  • Cancer within the past 5 years with the exception of excised basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma of the skin, or carcinoma in situ such as cervical or breast carcinoma that has been excised or resected completely andis without evidence of local recurrence or metastasis
     
  • Inflammatory scalp conditions (scalp psoriasis, dermatitis, tinea capitis)
     

  • Active systemic diseases that may cause hair loss (e.g., lupus , thyroiditis, systemic sclerosis, lichen planus, secondary syphilis)

     

  • History of autoimmune diseases other than AA  requiring systemic topical immunotherapy (e.g psoriasis)
     

  • Major surgery within 8 weeks prior to randomisation

     

  • Unstable psychiatric conditions (Schizophrenia, unstable bipolar disorder etc)

elements.name: refer
elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: question48
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
